title: Keeping FREE depths raised the Mw 6.5 share by 2.71 points in region-and-era-matched shallow GCMT Mw 5.8+ events in 1982-2020
abstract: We tested whether keeping only centroid depths marked FREE changes the magnitude mix in Global CMT. We used a fixed 1976-2020 catalog and selected 5,915 events in 1982-2020 with reference depth below 70 km and Mw at least 5.8. Common 10-degree cells and two catalog eras retained 4,406 events. With pooled stratum weights, the Mw 6.5-or-larger share was 19.09% for all depth flags and 21.80% for FREE depths. The increase was 2.71 percentage points, with a conditional 95% spatial-cell resampling interval of 1.34 to 4.11. The early-era increase was 4.75 points; the later-era interval included zero. An added reference-depth match retained a positive contrast in a smaller sample. Thus, the FREE filter changes this catalog target even after coarse region and era matching. This is a selection effect, not evidence that FREE depths are more accurate or that true event dynamics changed. Source depth, catalog methods, event clusters and incomplete spatial overlap limit inference. The package has original code, aggregate evidence, a figure and exact source retrieval checks. External event data remain outside the publication.

display.caption: The FREE filter raises the large-event share in the primary common-support sample. Points show FREE minus all depth flags. Lines show conditional 95% spatial-cell resampling intervals. Each check has its own common support. The added depth match was not in the initial plan.

citations.reason: Motivates an audit of depth flags. We use new code and the shared raw snapshot, not its bundled records.
Its FREE-only sensitivity result motivates care with sample changes.
